anyOf.description:
An empty object (`{}`). Removes the conferencing details from the event. You must also remove
the corresponding conference information from the event `description` in the same request.

event_description.title: Event description
event_description.description:
A brief description of the event (for example, its agenda). Nylas might return the description as
an HTML string, depending on how the provider formats it.

For Google accounts, this field accepts a maximum of 8,192 characters.

event_hide_participants.title: Hide participants on event
event_hide_participants.description: When `true`, hides the event's list of participants.

event_location.title: Event location
event_location.description: The location of the event (for example, a physical address or the name of a meeting room).

comment.description: A note or comment about the participant (for example, their nickname). If the participant's email address is missing, this field is also missing.

email.description:
The participant's email address.
For Microsoft Graph, this field can be missing.

name.description: The participant's full name.

phone_number.description: The participant's phone number. If the participant's email address is missing, this field is also missing.

event_reminders_create.title: Create reminders list
event_reminders_create.description: A list of reminders to send for the event. If left empty or omitted, the event uses the provider defaults.

use_default.title: Use Default
use_default.description:
When `true`, the event uses the calendar's default reminder settings.

- **Google**: Generates a `popup`-style reminder 10 minutes before the event begins.
- **Microsoft**: Generates a reminder 15 minutes before the event begins.
- **iCloud**: Does not generate a reminder.
- **EWS**: Generates a `display`-style reminder 15 minutes before the event begins.

overrides.title: Overrides
overrides.description:
A list of reminders for the event to use when `use_default` is `false`. If this field is empty
or omitted, and `use_default` is `false`, the event does not send reminders. If `true`, Nylas
generates both the default event reminder and any reminders in the `overrides` list.

You cannot set reminder overrides if `use_default` is `true`.

For Microsoft Graph, EWS, and iCloud, you can set only one reminder per event.

reminder_minutes.description: The number of minutes before the event start time when a user wants to receive a reminder for this event.

reminder_method.description:
(Google and iCloud only) The method used to notify the user about the event, with separate
options and default settings for each provider.

- **Google**:
  - Default: `popup`
  - Options: `popup`, `email`
- **iCloud**:
  - Default: `display`
  - Options: `display`, `sound`

event_time.title: Time
event_time.description: A specific point in time (for example, the start time of an event).

time.description: The time that the meeting occurs, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

timezone.description:
The timezone of the event as an
[IANA-formatted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones) string. If
populated, Nylas reads the value of `time` with the provided timezone.

event_when.title: When
event_when.description:
An object that represents the time and duration of an event.

You can format `when` as one of four sub-objects: `time`, `timespan`, `date`, or `datespan`. These
sub-objects allow you to capture and represent specific points in time.

`time` and `timespan` objects include optional timezone support.

status.description: A participant's RSVP status for the event.

resource_building.title: Resource Building
resource_building.description: The building where the room is located. For Google, this is the building ID rather than its display name.

resource_capacity.title: Resource Capacity
resource_capacity.description: The number of people the room can seat. Always returned, and `0` when the provider has no capacity for the room.

resource_email.title: Resource Email
resource_email.description: The email address associated with the room resource.

resource_floor_name.title: Resource Floor Name
resource_floor_name.description: The name of the floor where the room is located.

resource_floor_number.title: Resource Floor Number
resource_floor_number.description: (Microsoft only) The floor number where the room is located. Omitted when it's `0` or not set.

resource_floor_section.title: Resource Floor Section
resource_floor_section.description: (Google only) The section of the floor where the room is located.

resource_name.title: Resource Name
resource_name.description: The display name of the room resource. Omitted when the provider doesn't return one.

contact_company_name.title: Contact Company Name
contact_company_name.description: The name of the company that the contact is affiliated with (for example, their workplace).

contact_email.title: Contact email
contact_email.description:
An array of the contact's email addresses. Different providers may have different limits on the
number of email addresses.

- iCloud: multiple email addresses per contact.
- IMAP/Yahoo: at most one email address per contact.
- Microsoft/EWS: at most three email addresses per contact.

See [Contacts limitations](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contacts-limitations) for more information.

email.description: The contact's email address.

type.description: (Google, IMAP, iCloud, and Yahoo only) The email address type.

contact_im_address.title: Contact IM address
contact_im_address.description:
An array of the contact's instant messaging (IM) addresses. Different providers may have different
limits on the number of IM addresses.

- iCloud/Yahoo: multiple IM addresses per contact.
- IMAP: at most one IM address per contact.
- Microsoft/EWS: at most three IM addresses per contact.

See [Contacts limitations](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contacts-limitations) for more information.

type.description: The protocol for the IM address.

contact_job_title.title: Contact Job Title
contact_job_title.description: The contact's occupation or job title.

contact_manager_name.title: Contact Manager Name
contact_manager_name.description:
The name of the contact's manager. Native iCloud and Yahoo CardDAV contacts don't support this
field. See [Contacts limitations](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contacts-limitations) for more information.

contact_nickname.title: Contact Nickname
contact_nickname.description: A custom nickname for the contact.

contact_notes.title: Contact Notes
contact_notes.description: Notes about with the contact (for example, their favorite food).

contact_office_location.title: Contact Office Location
contact_office_location.description:
The location of the office where the contact works. Native iCloud and Yahoo CardDAV contacts don't
support this field. See [Contacts limitations](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contacts-limitations) for more
information.

contact_phone_number.title: Contact phone number
contact_phone_number.description:
An array of phone numbers associated with the contact. Different providers may have different limits
on the number of phone numbers.

- iCloud/Yahoo: multiple phone numbers per contact.
- IMAP: at most one phone number per contact.
- Microsoft: at most two home phone numbers, two work phone numbers, and one mobile phone number.
- EWS: at most two home phone numbers, two work phone numbers, one mobile phone number, and one
  other phone number.

See [Contacts limitations](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contacts-limitations) for more information.

number.description:
The contact's phone number, including its
[country code](https://www.itu.int/oth/T0202.aspx?parent=T0202).

type.description:
The phone number type. `mobile` is supported for Google, Microsoft Graph, iCloud, and Yahoo.
`other` is supported for Google, EWS, iCloud, and Yahoo.

contact_physical_address.title: Contact physical address
contact_physical_address.description:
An array of physical addresses associated with the contact. Different providers may have different
limits on the number of physical addresses.

- iCloud/Yahoo: multiple physical addresses per contact.
- IMAP: at most one physical address per contact.
- Microsoft/EWS: at most one physical address per contact per type.

See [Contacts limitations](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contacts-limitations) for more information.

city.description: The town or city in which the contact is located.

country.description: The country in which the contact is located.

postal_code.description: The postal code of a location associated with the contact.

state.description: The state or province in which the contact is located.

street_address.description: The street address of a location associated with the contact (for example, their work).

contact_picture_url.title: Contact Picture URL
contact_picture_url.description:
A URL that links to the contact's picture. Native iCloud and Yahoo CardDAV contacts don't support
profile pictures. See [Contacts limitations](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contacts-limitations) for more
information.

contact_source.title: Contact source
contact_source.description:
The source of the contact. See [Contact sources](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contact-sources) for
provider-specific availability and behavior.

contact_suffix.title: Contact Suffix
contact_suffix.description: (Not supported for EWS) The suffix of a contact's name, if applicable.

url.description: A URL that links to the contact's website.

emails.description: The contact's email addresses. May be `null` if the contact has no email addresses. Treat `null` the same as an empty array.

groups.description:
The contact's explicit provider-backed group memberships. Address-book containers and aggregate
views such as iCloud All Contacts are not groups. May be `null` if the contact has no group
memberships. Treat `null` the same as an empty array.

im_addresses.description: The contact's IM addresses. May be `null` if the contact has no IM addresses. Treat `null` the same as an empty array.

phone_numbers.description: The contact's phone numbers. May be `null` if the contact has no phone numbers. Treat `null` the same as an empty array.

physical_addresses.description: The contact's physical addresses. May be `null` if the contact has no physical addresses. Treat `null` the same as an empty array.

web_pages.description: The contact's web pages. May be `null` if the contact has no web pages. Treat `null` the same as an empty array.

contact_picture.title: Contact Picture
contact_picture.description:
The contact's picture, represented as a Base64-encoded string. Native iCloud and Yahoo CardDAV
contacts don't support profile pictures. See
[Contacts limitations](/docs/v3/email/contacts/#contacts-limitations) for more information.

application_id.description: The application ID that owns this configuration.

scope.description:
The scope of a configuration exposed by the public configuration endpoints.
Grant configurations carry dispatch_disabled_until and never contribute settings.
Calendar, recurring-series, and per-Notetaker configurations are managed through
sync endpoints and are not included in the public configuration list.

display_name.description: A human-readable name for this configuration.

deduplication_policy.description:
Controls whether Notetakers governed by this configuration participate in
deduplication. `active` and `inactive` are available on application and workspace
configurations. `inherit` and `disable` are available on calendar, event, and
per-notetaker configurations.

dispatch_disabled_until.description:
An RFC 3339 timestamp that suppresses Notetaker dispatch while it's in the future.
While suppression is active, Nylas rejects immediate join requests and doesn't
dispatch scheduled Notetakers governed by this configuration. `null` means dispatch
is enabled; a past timestamp means the suppression has expired. Only application,
workspace, and grant configurations accept this field. See
[Pause Notetaker dispatch](/docs/v3/notetaker/dispatch-suppression/).

version.description: The version number, incremented on each update.

created_at.description: When the configuration was created, in Unix timestamp seconds.

updated_at.description: When the configuration was last updated, in Unix timestamp seconds.

app_id.description:
The ID of the Nylas application associated with the template. Returned only if the template is
configured at the application level.

body.description: The body content of the template, in HTML format.

created_at.description: When the template was created, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

grant_id.description:
The ID of the grant associated with the template. Returned only if the template is configured
at the grant level.

id.description: The template ID.

name.description: The name of the template.

subject.description: The subject line of the template.

updated_at.description: When the template was last updated, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

workflow.description: A custom workflow that sends messages from a template when certain events are triggered.

app_id.description:
The ID of the Nylas application associated with the workflow. Returned only if the
workflow is configured at the application level.

date_created.description: When the workflow was created, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

delay.description:
The number of minutes between a `trigger_event` being met and the workflow sending
a message.

grant_id.description:
The ID of the grant associated with the workflow. Returned only if the workflow is
configured at the grant level.

id.description: The ID of the workflow.

is_enabled.description: When `true`, indicates that the workflow is enabled.

name.description: The name of the workflow.

template_id.description: The ID of the email template the workflow uses.

trigger_event.description:
The event which triggers the workflow.

`grant.expired` and `grant.deleted` require a `from` sender address, because the grant that
triggered them can no longer send email. Every other trigger accepts a workflow without one.

Workflows have no condition or filter field, so an enabled workflow sends for every matching
event in its scope. High-volume triggers such as `message.created` fire for every message in
every mailbox the workflow covers.

from.description: Details of the sender if the workflow uses transactional send.

email.description: The email address of the sender.

name.description: The name of the sender.

configuration_appearance.title: appearance
configuration_appearance.description: Appearance settings definitions for the Scheduling Page.

your-key.description: A key-value pair. For pre-defined keys for hosted Scheduling Pages, see [Styling options for hosted Scheduling Pages](/docs/v3/scheduler/customize-scheduler/#styling-options-for-hosted-scheduling-pages).

configuration_availability_open_hours.description: Open hours settings for a participant.
configuration_availability_open_hours.title: Open Hours

days.description: The days of the week that the open hour settings are applied to. Sunday corresponds to `0`, and Saturday corresponds to `6`.

start.description: The start time in 24-hour time format. Single-digit hours doesn't have a leading zero. The earliest start time is `0:00`, and the latest start time is `23:49`.

end.description: The end time in a 24-hour time format. Single-digit hours doesn't have a leading zero.

timezone.description:
The timezone for this open-hours block, as an [IANA-formatted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database) string.

For participant `open_hours`, this value applies only to the open-hours block where you define it and overrides the participant's `timezone`. If you omit it, Scheduler uses the participant's `timezone`, then `event_booking.timezone`.

For `default_open_hours` in Scheduler configurations, set `event_booking.timezone` to control the timezone that Scheduler uses when evaluating default open hours.

exdates.description: A list of dates that are excluded from the open hours. Dates should be formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

configuration_availability_rules.description: Availability rules for the scheduling configuration. These rules define how Nylas calculates availability for all participants.

availability_method.description:
The method that Nylas uses to calculate availability for all participants. For one-on-one
meetings, the `availability_method` is always `collective`.

The round-robin methods, `max-fairness` and `max-availability`, don't support
[Agent Account](/docs/v3/scheduler/agent-accounts/) participants. Use connected grants for
round-robin pools.

buffer.description: The amount of buffer time to add around existing meetings, in minutes. For example, if an account has a meeting scheduled from 10–11a.m., and you set a buffer of 30 minutes, Nylas treats 9:30–11:30a.m. as busy.

default_open_hours.description: A default set of open hours to apply to participants that don't define participant-level `open_hours`. You can overwrite these open hours for individual participants by specifying `open_hours` on the participant object. In Scheduler configurations, set `event_booking.timezone` to control the timezone used when Scheduler evaluates default open hours.

default_specific_time_availability.description:
Default specific date and time availability that applies to ALL participants in this configuration.
These are merged with participant-specific entries, with participant entries taking precedence
for the same date. Use this to define organization-wide special hours (e.g., holidays, events).

start.description:
The start time in HH:MM format (24-hour clock).
Use "00:00" with end "00:00" to mark the date as closed/unavailable.

end.description: The end time in HH:MM format (24-hour clock).

timezone.description:
The timezone for this specific date entry (e.g., "America/New_York").
Required when using default_specific_time_availability to ensure proper timezone conversion
across participants. When specified, `event_booking.timezone` must also be set.

only_specific_time_availability.description:
When `true`, ALL participants will ONLY be available at times defined in `default_specific_time_availability`
and their individual `specific_time_availability` entries. Regular `open_hours` and `default_open_hours`
are completely ignored.

This is useful for:
- Temporary availability windows (e.g., hiring events, special booking periods)
- Disabling all availability by setting to `true` with no specific dates defined

**Note**: When set at the config level, individual participants cannot override this to `false`.

configuration_availability.description: The rules that determine the available time slots for the event.

duration_minutes.description: The total number of minutes the event should last.

interval_minutes.description: The interval between meetings. Nylas checks from the nearest interval of the passed `start_time`. For example, you schedule 30-minute meetings (`duration_minutes`) with 15 minutes between them (`interval_minutes`). If you have a meeting starting at 9:59, the API returns times starting at 10:00 (10:00-10:30, 10:15-10:45).

round_to.description: Nylas rounds each time slot to the nearest `round_to` value. For example, if a time slot starts at 9:05a.m. and `round_to` is set to `15`, Nylas rounds it to 9:15a.m. Must be a multiple of 5 minutes.

booking_type.description:
The booking type. If set to `booking`, Scheduler follows the
[standard booking flow](/docs/v3/scheduler/customize-booking-flows/).

If set to `organizer-confirmation`, Scheduler creates an event marked "Pending" in the organizer's
calendar and sends a confirmation request email to the organizer. The confirmation request email
includes a link to a page where the organizer can confirm or cancel the booking.

description.description: The description of the event.

disable_emails.description:
When `true`, Nylas doesn't send email notifications when an event is booked, cancelled, or
rescheduled. When `null`, the default behavior applies (emails are sent).

hide_participants.description: When `true`, Nylas creates the event with `hide_participants=true`, so the host can see who's on the event but the guests cannot. When `null`, the default behavior applies (participants are visible).

notify_participants.description:
When `true`, the calendar provider sends notifications to participants when the
event is created, updated, or deleted. Microsoft grants ignore this flag and
always notify participants. This field may be `null` if not explicitly set on
the configuration; treat `null` the same as `false` (the default behavior).

email_subject.description: (Email reminders only) The subject line of the email reminder.

minutes_before_event.description: The number of minutes before the event to send the reminder. Must be a multiple of 5.

recipient.description: (Email reminders only) Who should receive the reminder.

timezone.description:
The timezone Nylas uses to display times in confirmation messages and reminders. This must be
an [IANA-formatted string](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database).

configuration_participants_availability.description: The availability data for the participant. If omitted, the participant is considered to be available at all times. At least one participant must have availability data.

calendar_ids.description:
A list of calendar IDs associated with the participant's email address. These calendars are
used to check the participant's availability.

For an [Agent Account](/docs/v3/scheduler/agent-accounts/) participant, set this to
`["primary"]` or to the Agent Account's email address. Scheduler reads busy time from an Agent
Account's primary calendar only.

open_hours.description: An array of objects for the participant's open hours. Nylas searches for free time slots within these open hours.

configuration_participants_booking.description: The booking data for the participant. If omitted, the participant is not included in the booked event. At least one participant must have booking data.

calendar_id.description:
The calendar ID that the event is created in.

For an [Agent Account](/docs/v3/scheduler/agent-accounts/) participant, set this to
`primary` or the Agent Account's email address. Scheduler creates booking events on an Agent
Account's primary calendar only.

configuration_participants_specific_time.description:
A specific date and time range when the participant is available.
Use "00:00" for both start and end to explicitly mark a date as unavailable.

start.description:
The start time in HH:MM format (24-hour clock).
Use "00:00" with end "00:00" to explicitly mark this date as unavailable.

end.description: The end time in HH:MM format (24-hour clock).

timezone.description:
The timezone for this specific date (e.g., "America/New_York").
Optional for participant-level entries. Uses the participant's timezone if not specified.

configuration_participants.description: List of participants for the scheduling Configuration.

email.description:
The participant's email address.

If the participant provides an `availability` or `booking` block, this email address must be
associated with a valid Nylas grant, or the request fails. Participants supplied by email only
(no `availability` or `booking` block) don't require a grant. They're treated as notification-only
invitees: they still receive scheduling emails, but they don't affect availability or free-busy
calculation and can't be selected as a round-robin host.

is_organizer.description:
When `true`, indicates that the participant is the organizer of the event.

For non-round-robin meetings, one of the participants must be specified as the organizer. For
round-robin meetings, remove the `is_organizer` key/value pair or set `is_organizer` to `false`
for all participants.

name.description: The participant's name.

only_specific_time_availability.description:
When `true`, this participant will ONLY be available at times defined in their
`specific_time_availability` entries. Their regular `open_hours` are ignored.

If the config-level `availability_rules.only_specific_time_availability` is `true`,
this participant-level setting cannot override it to `false`.

Setting to `true` with an empty `specific_time_availability` array results in
zero availability for this participant (useful for temporarily disabling someone).

timezone.description:
The timezone in which the participant is located, as an
[IANA-formatted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database) string. Nylas uses this when
calculating the participant's open hours, and in email notifications.

If a participant `open_hours` block includes its own `timezone`, the open-hours timezone
overrides this participant timezone for that block. If participant `open_hours` doesn't include
a `timezone`, Scheduler uses this participant timezone, then `event_booking.timezone`.

configuration_scheduler_additional_field.description: The definitions for additional fields in the Scheduler UI. Guests see every field on the scheduling page when they book an event, except fields with `type: metadata`.

label.description: The text label to be displayed in the Scheduler UI.

type.description: The field type. A `metadata` field is hidden from the guest: it doesn't appear on the booking form or in Scheduler's email notifications. When a guest submits the booking form, the Scheduler UI sends the field's `default` value with the booking, and booking webhooks include it in `booking_info.additional_fields`.

required.description: Whether the guest must fill in the field when booking an event. `POST /v3/scheduling/bookings` doesn't check it.

default.description:
The default value for the field. 

- For the `metadata` type, this field stores the value. The Scheduler UI sends it with each booking. `POST /v3/scheduling/bookings` doesn't, so pass the value in the request's `additional_fields`.
- For other types, this field sets the default value in the form, which is pre-filled when a guest books an event.

pattern.description: A regular expression pattern that the value of the field must match. `POST /v3/scheduling/bookings` doesn't check it.

order.description: The order in which the field will be displayed in the Scheduler UI. Fields with lower order values will be displayed first.

options.description: A list of options for the `dropdown` or `radio_button` types. This field is required for the `dropdown` and `radio_button` types.

configuration_scheduler_email_template_b.description: Configurable settings specifically for booking confirmed emails.

title.description: The title to replace the default 'Booking Confirmed' title. This doesn't change the email subject line. Only visible in emails sent to guests.

body.description: The additional body to be appended after the default body. Only visible in emails sent to guests.

logo.description:
The URL of a custom logo that is displayed at the top of the booking email. Replaces the default
Nylas logo. The URL needs to be publicly accessible.

show_nylas_branding.description: When `true`, displays Nylas branding in the booking email.

available_days_in_future.description: The number of days in the future that Scheduler is available for scheduling events.

min_booking_notice.description: The minimum number of minutes in the future that a user can make a new booking. This field may be `null` if not explicitly set on the configuration; treat `null` the same as `60` (the default behavior).

min_cancellation_notice.description: The minimum number of minutes before a booking can be cancelled.

cancellation_policy.description: A message about the cancellation policy to display to users when booking an event.

rescheduling_url.description: The URL used to reschedule bookings. This URL is included in confirmation messages.

cancellation_url.description: The URL used to cancel bookings. This URL is included in confirmation messages.

organizer_confirmation_url.description:
The URL used to confirm or cancel pending bookings. This URL is included in booking request
messages.

confirmation_redirect_url.description: The URL that Nylas redirects the user to when the booking is confirmed.

hide_rescheduling_options.description: If `true`, the option to reschedule an event is hidden in booking confirmations and email notifications.

hide_cancellation_options.description: If `true`, the option to cancel an event is hidden in booking confirmations and email notifications.

hide_additional_guests.description: Whether to hide the **Additional guests** field on the Scheduling Page. If `true`, guests cannot invite additional guests to the event.

notetaker_settings.description:
Settings for automatically adding a Notetaker bot to bookings created with this configuration.
When enabled, Notetaker joins the meeting to record, transcribe, and optionally generate
summaries and action items. Requires `event_booking.conferencing` to be configured.

enabled.description:
When `true`, automatically creates a Notetaker bot for bookings made with this configuration.
The bot joins the meeting at the scheduled time to record and transcribe.

show_ui_consent_message.description:
When `true`, displays a consent message in the Scheduler UI informing guests that the
meeting will be recorded.

notetaker_name.description:
The display name for the Notetaker bot that joins the meeting.
Maximum 255 characters. Required when `enabled` is `true`.

appearance.description:
An object that defines the appearance settings for the Scheduling Page. This field
may be `null` if no appearance customization has been set.

name.description: The name of the Scheduling Page. If not defined, Nylas defaults to the organizer's name.

participants.description:
A list of participants to be included in the scheduled event.

Participants that provide availability (through an `availability` or `booking` block) must be
associated with a valid Nylas grant, or the request fails. Participants supplied by email only
don't require a grant. They're notification-only invitees who receive scheduling emails but don't
affect availability calculation and can't be selected as a round-robin host.

This field isn't accepted for group or round-robin configurations, which are anchored to the
organizer's own grant and calendar instead.

requires_session_auth.description:
When `true`, the scheduling [Availability](/docs/reference/api/availability/) and
[Bookings](/docs/reference/api/bookings/) endpoints require a valid session ID to
authenticate requests using the specified Configuration. This field may be `null`
if not explicitly set on the configuration; treat `null` the same as `false`
(the default behavior).

slug.description:
The slug for the Configuration object. This is an optional, unique identifier. You can use the
slug instead of the `configuration_id` when making requests to the Nylas Scheduling endpoints.
Slugs are unique to each Nylas application. This field may be `null` if no slug has been set.

booking_type.description:
The booking type. Group Configurations support `booking` only, and follow the
[standard booking flow](/docs/v3/scheduler/customize-booking-flows/).

calendar_id.description:
The ID of the calendar on which the group event is created. Nylas doesn't support read-only
calendars.

disable_emails.description:
When `true`, Nylas doesn't send email notifications when an event is booked, cancelled, or
rescheduled. When `null`, the default behavior applies (emails are sent).

reminders.description: A list of reminders for the event.

email_subject.description: (Email reminders only) The subject line for the email reminder.

minutes_before_event.description: The number of minutes before the event to send the reminder.

recipient.description: (Email reminders only) Who should receive the email reminder.

name.description: The name of the Scheduling Page.

requires_session_auth.description:
When `true`, the [Availability](/docs/reference/api/availability/) and
[Bookings](/docs/reference/api/bookings/) endpoints require a valid session ID to
authenticate requests using the specified Configuration. This field may be `null`
if not explicitly set on the configuration; treat `null` the same as `false`
(the default behavior).

slug.description:
The slug for the Configuration object. This is an optional, unique identifier. You can use the
slug instead of the `configuration_id` when making requests to the Nylas Scheduling endpoints.
Slugs are unique to each Nylas application. This field may be `null` if no slug has been set.

type.description:
The type of event supported by the Configuration. When set to `group`, enables access to the
[Group Events endpoints](/docs/reference/api/group-events/) and functionality.
Defaults to empty (`""`) for all existing Configurations.

group_event_participants.title: Group event participants
group_event_participants.description:
An array of participants to include in the event booking. If you don't specify at least
one participant, Nylas uses the event organizer instead.

name.description: The participant's name.

email.description: The participant's email address.

is_organizer.description: When `true`, indicates that the participant is the event organizer.

group_event_recurrence.title: Group event recurrence settings
group_event_recurrence.description:
An array of `RRULE` and `EXDATE` strings. Nylas includes this field only if the event is the main
(master) event. See [RFC-5545](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5545#section-3.8.5) for more details.
You can use [this tool](https://jkbrzt.github.io/rrule/) to learn more about the `RRULE` spec.

Events inherit their timezone from the `when` object. Nylas recommends that you use the `when`
object to specify the event's start and end time.

Provider specifics:
  - Agent Accounts and virtual calendars don't support `DTSTART` or `TZID`. Nylas uses the event's `when` values as the start of the series instead.
  - iCloud accounts do _not_ support recurring events for group events
  - Microsoft Graph adds one day to the `UNTIL` date.

capacity.description: (Not supported for EWS events) The maximum number of attendees allowed in the event.

description.description:
A brief description of the group event (for example, its agenda). Nylas might return the
description as an HTML string, depending on how the provider formats it.

For Google accounts, this field accepts a maximum of 8,192 characters.

location.description:
The location of the group event (for example, a physical address or the name of a meeting
room).
location.example: New York Public Library, Cave Room

when.description: The time and duration of the event.

oneOf.title: Read-only object
oneOf.description: Read-only placeholder. Returned only in responses.

imported_events.description: A list of event IDs representing successfully imported group events.

import_failed.description: A list of event IDs representing group events that Nylas couldn't import.

reason.description: The reason the event wasn't imported.

start_time.description: The event's start time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

end_time.description: The event's end time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

event_id.description:
(Group Configurations only, required) The ID of the existing group event the guest is joining. Use the
`event_id` from the time slot returned by
[Get availability](/docs/reference/api/availability/get-availability/). Without it, the request returns
`Event not found`.

For a recurring group event, this is the ID of the occurrence being booked, not the ID of the
recurring series. Pass the series ID in `master_id`.

master_id.description:
(Group Configurations only, required for recurring group events) The ID of the recurring series that
the occurrence in `event_id` belongs to. Use the `master_id` from the same time slot as `event_id`.
Omit it for non-recurring group events.

calendar_id.description:
(Group Configurations only, required) The ID of the calendar that holds the group event. Use the
`calendar_id` from the same time slot as `event_id`.

participants.description: An array of objects that include a list of participant email addresses from the Configuration object to include in the booking. If not provided, Nylas includes all participants from the Configuration object.

email.description: The participant's email address.

guest.description: Details about the guest that is creating the booking. The guest `name` and `email` are required.

email.description: The guest's email address.

name.description: The guest's name.

timezone.description:
The guest's timezone, used in email notifications. If not provided, Nylas uses the timezone from
the [Configuration object](/docs/reference/api/configurations/).

email_language.description: The language of the guest email notifications.

additional_guests.description: An array of objects that include a list of additional guest email addresses to include in the booking.

email.description: The additional guest's email address.

name.description: The additional guest's name.

additional_fields.description: A dictionary of additional field keys mapped to the values populated by the guest in the booking form.

booking_id.description: The unique ID of the booking.

event_id.description: The unique ID of the event object associated with the booking.

organizer.description: The participant that is designated as the organizer of the event.

email.description: The organizer's email address.

name.description: The organizer's name.

status.description: The current status of the booking.

description.description: The description of the event.

salt.description: The salt extracted from the booking reference embedded in the organizer confirmation link, encoded as a URL-safe base64 string (without padding).

status.description: The action to take on the pending booking.

cancellation_reason.description: The reason that the booking is being cancelled.

start_time.description: The event's start time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

end_time.description: The event's end time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar to access.

end_time.description: The event's end time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.\

event_id.description: The ID of the event to update.

master_id.description:
(Recurring group events only, required) The ID of the recurring series that the occurrence in
`event_id` belongs to. Use the `master_id` from the same time slot as `event_id`.

start_time.description: The event's start time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

job_id.description: An identifier for the migration job.

public_application_id.description: The ID of v3 application this job is running for.

status.description:
The state of the job.

- **Pending**: The job has been created, but not started. Batch clone runs only after the linked
snapshot job is completed.
- **Running**: The job is currently running.
- **Completed**: The job has successfully finished all migrations.
- **Failed**: _All_ migrations failed.
- **Partial**: The job successfully migrated _some_ accounts, but some could not be migrated or were created as "placeholder" grants.

count_all.description: A total number of accounts to be migrated. The total is a sum of the successful and failed migrations.

count_success.description: The number of accounts that were successfully migrated.

count_failed.description: The number of accounts that were unable to migrate.

count_warning.description: The number of accounts that were migrated as invalid grants ("placeholder" grant ready for re-authentication).

created_at.description: The time when the job was created, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

updated_at.description: The time the job was updated, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

linked_job_id.description: The bulk migration tool creates two separate jobs that run one after the other. This ID links them together.

v2_application_id.description: The ID of the v2 Nylas application the connected account belongs to.

v2_account_id.description: The ID of v2 connected account you are requesting translations for.

resource_type.description:
The names of the v2 resources you're requesting translations for.

To request Gmail's "labels", include `folders`. (Nylas v3 consolidates folders and labels into
one resource.)

translations.description:
A list of v2 Nylas IDs and their v3 Provider ID counterparts, according to the requested resource
type and v2 connected account.

next_page_number.description: A page number for next set of results, if more results are available. This field does not appear if there are no more results.

synced-calendars.description:
The calendar IDs to sync, from 1 to 50. Nylas syncs and sends `calendar.*` and `event.*`
notifications for these calendars only, starting from the grant's next sync. It checks every
ID against the grant's calendars before it saves anything, so use the provider's calendar IDs from
[`GET /v3/grants/{grant_id}/calendars`](/docs/reference/api/calendar/get-all-calendars/),
not `primary`. To remove the list, delete the setting instead of sending an empty array.

starred.description: Set to `true` to mark as starred; `false` to mark as not starred.

unread.description: Set to `true` to mark as unread; `false` to mark as read.

folders.description: The ID(s) of the folder(s) to apply, overwriting all folders previously associated with the message. Microsoft messages can be in a single folder only. Google allows a single message to appear in multiple folders.

message_id.description: An array of IDs for the messages Nylas will clean.

ignore_links.description: If `true`, removes link-related tags (`<a>`) from the message while keeping the text.

ignore_images.description: If `true`, removes images from the message.

images_as_markdown.description:
If `true`, converts images in the message to
[Markdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markdown). Can't be `false` when `html_as_markdown`
is `true`.

ignore_tables.description:
If `true`, removes table-related tags (`<table>`, `<th>`, `<td>`, `<tr>`) from the message
while keeping rows.

remove_conclusion_phrases.description: If `true`, removes phrases such as "Best" and "Regards" from the message signature.

html_as_markdown.description:
**This property is in beta**. If `true`, converts the message to
[Markdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markdown). Can't be `true` when
`images_as_markdown` is `false`.

attachments.description: An array of files to be sent with the message.

content.description:
The Base64-encoded file content. See
[Working with email attachments](/docs/v3/email/attachments/#attachment-schemas-and-size-limits)
for more information.

content_disposition.description:
(Not supported for Microsoft and EWS) The content disposition of the file. Usually,
this is `inline` or `attachment`, followed by the file name.

content_id.description: (Inline attachments only) The alphanumeric `cid` from the `` tag in the HTML message body. To avoid unexpected behavior in threads, make sure to use unique CIDs across messages of a thread.

content_type.description:
The
[MIME type](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Basics_of_HTTP/MIME_types/Common_types)
of the file. This is used by the email client to determine how to display the
attachment.

bcc.description: A list of people BCC'd on the message.

name.description: The name of the person BCC'd on the message.

email.description: The email address of the person BCC'd on the message.

body.description: The HTML body of the message.

cc.description: A list of people CC'd on the message.

name.description: The name of the person CC'd on the message.

email.description: The email address of the person CC'd on the message.

custom_headers.description: An array of custom headers to add to the message.

name.description: The header name.

from.description:
The sender of the message. Accepts a single object in an array. If omitted, Nylas uses the
grant's email address and display name.

name.description: The name of the user sending the message.

email.description: The email address of the user sending the message.

is_plaintext.description: When `true`, the message body is sent as plain text and the MIME data doesn't include the HTML version of the message. When `false`, the message body is sent as HTML.

reply_to.description: A list of people who should receive replies to the message by default.

name.description: The name of the person who should receive replies to the message.

email.description: The email address of the person who should receive replies to the message.

reply_to_message_id.description:
The ID of the message you're replying to. For Gmail and Microsoft Graph, this is the
message ID on the provider. For IMAP Send, this is the
[RFC822](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc822#section-4.6.1) `Message-ID` header
of the message you're replying to.

send_at.description:
The time when Nylas should send the message, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format. This time must be
at least one minute in the future from the time you make your request. You can schedule
a message to be sent up to 30 days in the future. If the request includes
`tracking_options.domain_name`, Nylas validates the hostname when it creates the schedule
and revalidates it before delivery.

template.description: The [template](/docs/reference/api/application-level-templates/) to use for the message. Can be overriden by the `body` and `subject` fields.

id.description: The template ID.

strict.description:
When `true`, Nylas returns an error if the template contains variables that aren't
defined in the `variables` object.

variables.description:
A set of key/value pairs representing variables to substitute for values in the
template.

to.description: A list of people that the message will be sent to.

name.description: The name of the person the message will be sent to.

email.description: The email address of the person the message will be sent to.

tracking_options.description: Tracking settings for the message. See [Track messages](/docs/v3/email/message-tracking/).

opens.description:
When `true`, enables
[message open tracking](/docs/v3/email/message-tracking/#message-open-tracking) on the
message. Nylas generates a
[`message.opened` webhook notification](/docs/reference/notifications/#message-opened-notifications)
when a participant first opens the message.

thread_replies.description:
When `true`, enables
[thread replied tracking](/docs/v3/email/message-tracking/#thread-replied-tracking)
on the message. Nylas generates a
[`thread.replied` webhook notification](/docs/reference/notifications/#thread-replied-notifications)
when a participant replies to the thread.

links.description:
When `true`, enables
[link clicked tracking](/docs/v3/email/message-tracking/#link-clicked-tracking) on the
message. Nylas generates a
[`message.link_clicked` webhook notification](/docs/reference/notifications/#link-clicked-notifications)
when a participant clicks a link in the message.

label.description:
A brief description of the message, why it's being tracked, or the tracking options
enabled.

use_draft.description:
(Google and Microsoft only) When `true`, Nylas saves the message in the user's Drafts folder
until its `send_at` time. This field can't be `true` if `send_at` is undefined.

signature_id.description:
The ID of a [signature](/docs/v3/email/signatures/) to append to the message body. Nylas
inserts the signature after a line break at the end of the body, including after any quoted
text in replies and forwards. Only one signature can be used per message.

attachment.description: The content of the attachment (if available), in binary format.

bcc.description: A list of people BCC'd on the message.

name.description: The name of the person BCC'd on the message.

email.description: The email address of the person BCC'd on the message.

body.description: The HTML body of the message.

cc.description: A list of people CC'd on the message.

name.description: The name of the person CC'd on the message.

email.description: The email address of the person CC'd on the message.

custom_headers.description: An array of custom headers to add to the message.

name.description: The header name.

from.description:
The sender of the message. Accepts a single object in an array. If omitted, Nylas uses
the grant's email address and display name.

name.description: The name of the user sending the message.

email.description: The email address of the user sending the message.

is_plaintext.description: When `true`, the message body is sent as plain text and the MIME data doesn't include the HTML version of the message. When `false`, the message body is sent as HTML.

reply_to.description: A list of people who should receive replies to the message by default.

name.description: The name of the person who should receive replies to the message.

email.description: The email address of the person who should receive replies to the message.

send_at.description:
The time when Nylas should send the message, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.
Must be at least one minute in the future from the time you make your request. You can
schedule a message to be sent up to 30 days in the future. If the request includes
`tracking_options.domain_name`, Nylas validates the hostname when it creates the schedule
and revalidates it before delivery.

template.description: The [template](/docs/reference/api/application-level-templates/) to use for the message. Can be overriden by the `body` and `subject` fields.

id.description: The template ID.

strict.description:
When `true`, Nylas returns an error if the template contains variables that aren't
defined in the `variables` object.

variables.description:
A set of key/value pairs representing variables to substitute for values in the

oneOf.description: Single-host configuration for one-on-one bookings.

availability.description: The rules that determine available time slots for the event.

availability_rules.description: A list of availability rules that apply to all participants.

availability_method.description: The method Nylas uses to calculate availability for all participants.

buffer.description: A list of rules that set buffer time around events for all participants.

after.description:
The amount of buffer time to add after meetings. For example, if
an account has a meeting scheduled from 10:00–11:00a.m., and you
set an after buffer of 15 minutes, Nylas treats 10:00–11:15a.m. as
busy.

before.description:
The amount of buffer time to add before meetings. For example, if
an account has a meeting scheduled from 10:00–11:00a.m., and you
set a before buffer of 30 minutes, Nylas treats 9:30–11:00a.m. as
busy.

duration_minutes.description: The total duration of the event, in minutes.

interval_minutes.description: The interval between meetings, in minutes.

round_to.description:
Nylas rounds each time slot to the nearest `round_to` value. For example,
if a time slot starts at 9:05a.m. and `round_to` is set to 15, Nylas rounds
it to 9:15a.m.

event_booking.description: An object containing details about the booking.

disable_emails.description:
When `true`, Nylas doesn't send email notifications when an event is booked,
cancelled, or rescheduled. When `null`, the default behavior applies (emails are sent).

hide_participants.description: When `true`, Nylas creates the event with `hide_participants=true`, so the host can see who's on the event but the guests cannot. When `null`, the default behavior applies (participants are visible).

notify_participants.description:
When `true`, the calendar provider sends notifications to participants
when the event is created, updated, or deleted. Microsoft grants ignore
this flag and always notify participants. This field may be `null` if not
explicitly set on the configuration; treat `null` the same as `false`.

reminders.description: A list of reminders for the event.

minutes_before_event.description: The number of minutes before the event to send the reminder.

recipient.description: (Email reminders only) Who should receive the reminder.

timezone.description:
The event's timezone as an
[IANA-formatted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database) string.

id.description: The Configuration ID.

name.description: The name of the Scheduling Page.

participants.description: A list of participants included in the scheduled event.

availability.description: The availability settings for the participant.

calendar_ids.description: A list of calendar IDs used to check the participant's availability.

open_hours.description:
An array of objects representing the participant's open hours. Nylas
searches for free time slots within these open hours.

days.description:
The days of the week that the open hour settings are applied
to. Sunday corresponds to `0`, and Saturday corresponds to `6`.

end.description: The end time in 24-hour time format.

exdates.description:
A list of dates that are excluded from the participant's open
hours, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

start.description: The start time in 24-hour time format.

timezone.description:
The participant's timezone as an
[IANA-formatted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database)
string. Nylas uses this when calculating the participant's open
hours and in email notifications.

calendar_id.description: The ID of the calendar the event was created on.

email.description: The participant's email address.

name.description: The participant's name.

is_organizer.description: When `true`, shows that the participant is the organizer of the event.

requires_session_auth.description:
When `true`, the scheduling Availability and Bookings endpoints require a valid
session ID to authenticate requests using the Configuration. This field may be
`null` if not explicitly set; treat `null` the same as `false`.

additional_fields.description: An object containing additional custom fields.

label.description: The text label to be displayed in the Scheduler UI.

order.description:
The order in which the field is displayed in the Scheduler UI.
Fields with lower order values are displayed first.

required.description: When `true`, marks the field as required.

available_days_in_future.description:
The number of days in the future that Scheduler is available for scheduling
events.

body.description: The body text of the message.

min_booking_notice.description:
The minimum number of minutes in the future that a user can schedule a new
booking. This field may be `null` if not explicitly set; treat `null` the
same as `60`.

min_cancellation_notice.description:
The minimum amount of time before a meeting that the booking can still be
cancelled, in minutes.

slug.description:
The Configuration slug. You can use this instead of the `configuration_id`
when making requests to other Scheduling endpoints. This field may be `null`
if no slug has been set.

grant_settings_grant_id.name: grant_id
grant_settings_grant_id.description: ID of the grant to access.

limit.name: limit
limit.description:
The maximum number of objects to return. See [Pagination](/docs/reference/api/#pagination)
for more information.

metadata_pair.name: metadata_pair
metadata_pair.description:
Pass one indexed metadata key/value pair (for example, `?metadata_pair=key1:value`) to search for
objects. The key must be `key1`, `key2`, `key3`, `key4`, or `key5`. See
[Metadata](/docs/reference/api/#metadata) for more information.

page_token.name: page_token
page_token.description:
An identifier that specifies which page of data to return. You can get this value from the
`next_cursor` response field. See [Pagination](/docs/reference/api/#pagination) for more
information.

query_imap_list.name: query_imap
query_imap_list.description:
(IMAP, Yahoo, and iCloud only) When `true`, Nylas queries the IMAP server directly instead of the
Nylas database. You also need to set the `in` query parameter in your request so Nylas knows which
folder to query.

field_selection.name: select
field_selection.description:
Specify fields that you want Nylas to return, as a comma-separated list (for example,
`select=id,updated_at`). This allows you to receive only the portion of object data that you're
interested in. You can use `select` to optimize response size and reduce latency by limiting queries
to only the information that you need.

shared_folder_id.name: shared_folder_id
shared_folder_id.description:
(Microsoft only) When provided, Nylas returns items from the specified shared folder ID.
Required when using `shared_from`.
This parameter only accepts a single folder ID.
Check out the [Shared folders](/docs/provider-guides/microsoft/shared-folders) guide for more information.

shared_from.name: shared_from
shared_from.description:
(Microsoft only) When provided, Nylas returns items that were shared from the specified email address.
It also accepts grant ID.
This parameter only accepts single email address or grant ID.
Check out the [Shared folders](/docs/provider-guides/microsoft/shared-folders) guide for more information.

grant_id.name: grant_id
grant_id.description:
ID of the grant to access. You can also use the email address associated with the grant, or use `/me/`
to refer to the grant associated with an access token.

query_imap_get_by_id.name: query_imap
query_imap_get_by_id.description:
(IMAP, iCloud, and Yahoo only) When `true`, Nylas queries from the IMAP server directly instead of
the Nylas database.

hard_delete.name: hard_delete
hard_delete.description:
When `true`, Nylas immediately deletes the specified message instead of sending it to the user's Trash
folder. This operation is irreversible.

To use this query parameter, you need to turn on "Enable hard delete" in the
[Nylas Dashboard](https://dashboard.nylas.com/?utm_source=docs&utm_content=docs-hard-delete) under
**Customizations > API**.

include_hidden_folders.name: include_hidden_folders
include_hidden_folders.description: (Microsoft only) When `true`, Nylas includes hidden folders in its response.

parent_id.name: parent_id
parent_id.description: (Microsoft and EWS only) Use the ID of a folder to find all child folders it contains.

single_level.name: single_level
single_level.description: (Microsoft only) If `true`, retrieves folders from a single-level hierarchy only. If `false`, retrieves folders across a multi-level hierarchy.

attendees.name: attendees
attendees.description:
(Not supported for Agent Accounts or virtual calendars) Filter for events that include the specified attendees. This
parameter accepts a comma-delimited list of email addresses.

busy.name: busy
busy.description: (Not supported for iCloud) Filter for events with the specified `busy` status.

calendar_id.name: calendar_id
calendar_id.description:
Filter for the specified calendar ID.

(Not supported for iCloud) You can use `primary` to query the user's primary calendar.

For an [Agent Account](/docs/v3/agent-accounts/calendars/#address-the-primary-calendar-in-calendar_id), you can also pass the account's own email address, in any letter case, to query its primary calendar. Any other email address returns a `400` error.

description.name: description
description.description: Filter for events matching the specified description. The filter is case insensitive and will match partial descriptions.

end.name: end
end.description:
Filter for events that end at or before the specified time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format. For example, if
you filter for events that end at 5:00p.m., and the calendar includes an event that runs from
4:30–5:30p.m., Nylas returns that event.

Defaults to one month from the time you make the request.

The `end` value cannot be earlier than `start`. For iCloud accounts, the difference between `start`
and `end` can't be greater than one year.

event_type.name: event_type
event_type.description:
(Google only) Filter for events with the specified event type. You can pass this query parameter
multiple times to select or exclude multiple event types. For example,
`event_type=default&event_type=outOfOffice` returns all events that are default or `OOO`, and excludes
any events that are `focusTime` or that have a `workingLocation`.

If you don't specify an event type, Nylas uses `default` to filter for regular events that don't have
another specific type.

expand_recurring.name: expand_recurring
expand_recurring.description:
**This parameter is deprecated. Use the
[Import Events endpoint](/docs/reference/api/events/import-events/)
instead**.

When `true`, Nylas returns all recurring events within the specified time range, including individual
occurrences of the recurring event. Otherwise, Nylas only returns the parent event and any event
overrides (individual occurrences that have been edited) in the time range.

ical_uid.name: ical_uid
ical_uid.description:
(Not supported for iCloud) Filter for events with the specified `ical_uid`. You _cannot_ apply other
filters if you use this parameter.

location.name: location
location.description: Filter for events with the specified location. The filter is case insensitive and will match partial locations.

master_event_id.name: master_event_id
master_event_id.description:
(Not supported for iCloud) Filter for instances of recurring events with the specified `master_event_id`.

`master_event_id` is _not_ respected by metadata filtering.

When using `master_event_id` to fetch recurring events with a Google grant, the order of the results will not be sorted chronologically.
Instead, Nylas returns the unchanged occurrences first, followed by the modified occurrences.
For example, if you have a recurring event with the following occurrences:
- 2025-01-01
- 2025-01-02
- 2025-01-03

But you modify the time of the second occurrence to 2025-01-02, the results will be:
- 2025-01-01
- 2025-01-03
- 2025-01-02 (modified)

show_cancelled.name: show_cancelled
show_cancelled.description:
(Not supported for iCloud or EWS) If `true`, Nylas includes events whose `status` is `cancelled`.

Different providers have different semantics for cancelled events:

- **Google**: An event is considered cancelled after a user deletes it from their calendar, until
it's eventually hard-deleted and is no longer readable.
- **Microsoft**: An event is considered cancelled if the user is invited to an event and the
organizer deletes it. The cancelled version of the event stays on the participants' calendars until
they delete it manually.

start.name: start
start.description:
Filter for events that start at or after the specified time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format. For example, if
you filter for events that start at 9:00a.m., and the calendar includes an event that runs from
8:30–9:30a.m., Nylas returns that event.

Defaults to the time that you make the request.

The `start` value cannot be later than `end`. For iCloud accounts, the difference between `start`
and `end` can't be greater than one year.

tentative_as_busy.name: tentative_as_busy
tentative_as_busy.description: (Microsoft and EWS only) When `true`, Nylas treats tentative events as busy.

title.name: title
title.description: Filter for events that match the specified title. The filter is case insensitive and will match partial titles.

updated_after.name: updated_after
updated_after.description:
(Google, Microsoft, and EWS only) Filter for events that have been updated after the specified time,
in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

`updated_after` is _not_ respected by metadata filtering.

updated_before.name: updated_before
updated_before.description:
(Google, Microsoft, and EWS only) Filter for events that have been updated before the specified time,
in seconds using the Unix timestamp format.

`updated_before` is _not_ respected by metadata filtering.

notify_participants.name: notify_participants
notify_participants.description:
When `true`, the provider emails participants about the change. Set to `false` to make the
change without notifying participants.

Microsoft returns a `400` error for `notify_participants=false`. iCloud ignores the setting and
always notifies participants.

max_results.name: limit
max_results.description:
Specifies the maximum number of events Nylas returns in a single page of results. The actual number
of events Nylas returns might be lower than this limit, even if other events match your query
parameters.

calendar_id_no_validate.name: calendar_id
calendar_id_no_validate.description:
The calendar ID of the event.

For Microsoft, we do not validate whether the given calendar ID matches the real calendar ID of the event.
This is due to a limitation of the Microsoft Graph API.

(Not supported for iCloud) You can use `primary` to query the user's primary calendar.

For an [Agent Account](/docs/v3/agent-accounts/calendars/#address-the-primary-calendar-in-calendar_id), you can also pass the account's own email address, in any letter case, to query its primary calendar. Any other email address returns a `400` error.

skip_nylas_email.name: skip_nylas_email
skip_nylas_email.description: When `true`, Nylas does not send the RSVP email to the event organizer.

limit_contacts.name: limit
limit_contacts.description:
The maximum number of objects to return. See [Pagination](/docs/reference/api/#pagination)
for more information.

join_time_start.name: join_time_start
join_time_start.description:
Filter for Notetaker bots that have join times that start at or after a specific time, in Unix
timestamp format.

join_time_end.name: join_time_end
join_time_end.description:
Filter for Notetaker bots that have join times that end at or are before a specific time, in Unix
timestamp format.

notetaker_order_by.name: order_by
notetaker_order_by.description: The field to order the Notetaker bots by.

notetaker_order_direction.name: order_direction
notetaker_order_direction.description: The direction to order the Notetaker bots by.

notetaker_state.name: state
notetaker_state.description: Filter for Notetaker bots with the specified meeting state.

prev_page_token.name: prev_page_token
prev_page_token.description:
An identifier that specifies which page of data to return. You can get this value from the
`prev_cursor` response field. See [Pagination](/docs/reference/api/#pagination) for more
information.

offset.name: offset
offset.description:
The number of items to skip before starting to return results. Use with `limit`
to page through results.

config_id.name: config_id
config_id.description: The ID of the configuration to access.

config_include.name: include
config_include.description: When set to `history`, the response includes the version history of the configuration.

start_time.name: start_time
start_time.description:
Filter for events that start at or after the specified time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format. For example,
if you filter for events that start at 9:00a.m. and the calendar includes an event that runs from
8:30–9:30a.m., Nylas returns that event.

end_time.name: end_time
end_time.description:
Filter for events that end at or before the specified time, in seconds using the Unix timestamp format. For example,
if you filter for events that end at 5:00p.m. and the calendar includes an event that runs from
4:30–5:30p.m., Nylas returns that event.
